report:
Reviewed the complete expected_types claim, the ordinary expr.rs implementation association, the explicit TODO implementation association, and the sole TODO test entry. Captured the checking design, the relevant accepted architectural-foundations normalization decision, and the coercion helper dependency. Rust guidance was read in this review session. Source inspection only: no behavioral tests were run and no source changes were made.

The claim has three distinct obligations: an available expected type is supplied before checking beneath the boundary; expression forms may consume it for local inference and materialized coercion; it must not select trait-proof, method-provider or alias-normalization candidates. The ordinary source currently provides only an initial boundary. The direct-call branch synthesizes the callee, extracts FnPtr parameters with check_call_ty, and passes the matching parameter to check_with_expected before checking each argument; arguments without a known parameter are checked normally. The helper explicitly synthesizes the argument first and only then calls coerce_expr_or_original_with_context. It does not thread the expectation recursively into literals, closures, aggregates, or branch expressions. This limitation is accurately recorded in the associated TODO implementation explanation and is not treated as full bidirectional checking.

The captured coercion helper relates the synthesized expression type to its target, materializes supported NeverToAny conversions (including block-tail conversion), and preserves contextual diagnostics on failure. This is narrow supporting context, not proof of every conversion or recursive inference case. The method-call branch discovers a provider using the receiver, method name and checked argument types; the outer check_with_expected value is not passed into that discovery. The RFD independently requires normalization to produce and merge its own type answer before relating it to an expected result. These observations explain the intended separation, but do not substitute for the missing adversarial candidate-selection evidence.

The sole annotated test checking_body_expected_types has no assertions and is explicitly TODO. Its comment calls for source-driven cases covering representative call arguments, literals, closures, aggregate/branch elements, materialized completed-IR conversions, and incompatible expected types that must not disambiguate solver or method candidates. The prerequisite is completion of expression-specific expected-type consumption plus this claim-specific verification matrix, including alias-normalization independence. Both the implementation TODO and test TODO are justified by the visible post-synthesis-only helper. No runtime coverage or full claim completion is asserted. The ordinary association identifies partial work; it does not override the explicit implementation/evidence deferrals. All claim aspects and evidence entries are accounted for, with no additional requested edits.
